verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Alwar engineering units with a funded order book and a clean receivables record; avoid small job-work fabricators selling to state utilities and EPC contractors with stretched payables.
title: Alwar Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**An engineering unit in Alwar buys steel, castings and bought-out components, adds machining, fabrication or assembly, and sells either as an OEM supplier or as a job-worker to larger EPC and capital-goods buyers.** Cash comes in only after the buyer accepts the goods and pays, so the unit funds steel inventory and wages for weeks before a rupee returns. Pricing power sits with whoever holds the drawing and the customer relationship; the job-worker takes what the OEM offers. **So when a proposal lands, first ask who owns the drawing and who sets the price; if the borrower is a pure job-worker on a single buyer, treat it as a wage-earner with a balance sheet, not a manufacturer.**

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is the whole business: inventory of steel and work-in-progress, plus receivables from EPC buyers who themselves wait on project payments.** Rating commentary on the sector notes that EPC cash conversion cycles stay high because execution periods are long, while OEMs turn faster [11], and that a longer cycle simply means more working-capital funding [9]. Against it, Rajasthan's GST collections ran 4.7% lower Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and state electricity demand grew 4.0% against India's 9.5% [D] — both local stress signals. **So treat the district as a two-speed market: a new OEM cluster pulling in suppliers, and a wider state economy that is not expanding.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 machining and fabrication suppliers who have a purchase order or rate contract from the new engine plant or from listed capital-goods buyers, and whose order book is funded rather than bid for.** Peer results show the demand is real but margins are not automatic: Pitti is expanding on data-centre, mining and railway order visibility [4], DEE's revenue rose 77% to ₹286.7 crore with operating profit at ₹47.6 crore [5], Skipper reported its highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% [6], while Suzlon grew revenue 26% to ₹4,869 crore but saw EBITDA margin fall to 14.8% from 18.6% [7]. **So structure against the order book, not the optimism: sanction against confirmed POs, keep the drawing and buyer details on file, and take monthly stock-and-receivables statements plus the GST return each month.** Avoid units whose order book is dominated by state utility or EPC contracts with retention money and bank guarantees; bid guarantees and performance guarantees tie up limits before any cash arrives [9]. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch the buyer mix and the bank-guarantee book.** If a borrower's top buyer crosses half of sales, or guarantee limits are fully drawn while receivables age, the unit is financing someone else's project. **Ask for the monthly sales register and the guarantee utilisation; if either moves against you two months running, cut limits and move to cash-backed terms.**
